reports.note: A tornado carved a narrow southwest-to-northeast path through Keyes, beginning near Phillips Avenue and dissipating past Monroe Avenue. Along the way, it shifted an anchored mobile home, hurled an empty grain silo roughly 100 yards, and snapped utility poles and trees. The most severe destruction occurred near Polk Street, collapsing an old pool hall and tearing the roof and an exterior wall off an adjacent building. Because the majority of the structural damage impacted older, less sturdy buildings, the tornado received a lower rating. Tornado is rated EF1 with max winds rated around 100 mph.

A tornado developed in the Via Caballero neighborhood in the south central portion of Santa Fe just north of I-25. The tornado traveled northward for approximately 1.4 miles, terminating near the College of Santa Fe. Much of the damage was along Rancho Siringo and Camino Chueco Roads. Damage included broken power poles, uprooted or damaged trees, damage to roofs. Ten homes sustained damaged. This tornado has been given a preliminary rating of EF-1, pending additional information.

tracks.note: A tornado developed south of I-25 with more impactful damage starting in the Via Caballero neighborhood in the south central portion of Santa Fe just north of I-25. The tornado traveled northward for approximately 2.25 miles, terminating near the College of Santa Fe. Much of the damage was along Rancho Siringo and Camino Chueco Roads. Damage included broken power poles, uprooted or damaged trees, damage to roofs. Ten homes sustained damaged with one home having the majority of the roof removed and a collapsed wall. This tornado has been given a rating of EF-1 with peak winds of 110 mph.

Here it snapped a few branches off of some elm trees and did damage to an older mobile home by pushing it a few feet, despite being anchored down. The tornado then continued northeast where it lifted an empty grain silo and either rolled or tossed or a combination of both across a field and landed about 100 yards or so to the northeast. It also snapped the top of a power pole. The tornado continued northeast  It caused some minor roof damage to the community center, including the collapse of one of the walls and destroyed the sidewalk awning connecting the two buildings. Another power pole was also broken in a couple of spots. This location likely had an enhancement of wind due to the enclosed nature of the area. A very brief tornado moved across a farmstead approximately 5 miles northeast of Madison, resulting in a broken tree and other minor tree damage.

NWS Storm Survey found damage consistent with a brief tornado west of Clark in rural southern Randolph County around 10:42 am on Tuesday, November 3rd.  The tornado began near the intersection of Route B and County Road 2690, moving to the north northeast where it damaged a farmstead along 2690, inflicting damage to trees and farm outbuildings. The tornado ended near the intersection of County Roads 2690 and D234. The max estimated wind speeds were around 90 mph. The tornado traveled around 1 mile in length, was 50 yards in width, and was on the ground for around 2 minutes.

Around 10:17am on November 3rd, 2026, a mini supercell developed out ahead of a quasi-linear convective system (QLCS) near the Texas and Louisiana border to the west of Mooringsport, LA. This mini supercell produced a very brief EF-0 tornado that touched down on Parish Road 136 between the Black Bayou and Highway 49. The tornado downed a large hardwood tree along this Parish Road as it then continued northeast towards Highway 49. Before the tornado reached Highway 49, it moved across the intersection of Parish Road 136 and Gamm Road, where a storm spotter captured a geotagged photo of the tornado lifting just west of Highway 49.  The storm survey team consulted numerous residents, law enforcement officials, and utility workers to help determine whether the tornado track continued beyond Highway 49 after witnessing a lack of additional damage, and these conversations led the team to conclude that there was no additional damage from this storm. This weak tornado, originating from a quasi-linear convective system, began just south of Holmes Road in far northwestern DeSoto Parish in a rural and wooded area. It then continued northeastward in a predominantly rural area, crossing into far southwestern Caddo Parish and ending just west of Four Forks Road and south of the Four Forks community.  Despite the radar showing a few tornadic debris signatures, the damage was confined to relatively light tree damage with no tree snaps or uproots. This limited the survey team's rating to an EF-0.

This same thunderstorm line segment advanced northeast, prompting a few tornado warnings in Shreveport and Bossier City. A tornadic debris signature was noted near Bert Kouns Road, approximately 3 miles south-southeast of the Shreveport Airport.  However, the NWS survey team could not find ratable damage there.
